proof:
# Power concavity after optimizing the integer tilt of two endpoints

Let d>=1 and let A,C be convex bodies in R^d with volumes 0<a<=c.
Fix a unit continuous direction u. Write

    A(t)=|A intersect {u.x>=t}|,
    C(t)=|C intersect {u.x>=t}|,
    K(t)=inf_v [A(t+v)+C(t-v)].                         (1)

This is exactly the endpoint contribution minimized over the integer
normal of an ambient cap through the middle fiber. The following is an
exact one-direction property, not a common transported measure or a
claim about cross-direction compatibility.

## 1. Quantile formula

For 0<=s<=a let q_A(s) be the unique cap threshold with cap volume s,
using the maximum and minimum support values at s=0,a. Define q_C on
[0,c] similarly. Then for 0<r<a,

    q_K(r)=(1/2) min_(0<=s<=r)[q_A(s)+q_C(r-s)]        (2)

is the unique threshold with K(q_K(r))=r.

First, 0<=K<=a, by sending v to negative infinity in (1). The infimum
can be taken over a compact interval for bounded t, by saturating the
two caps once their thresholds pass the support endpoints. Thus K is
continuous. To prove (2), let q denote its right side. If t<=q, then
A(p)+C(2t-p)>=r for every p. If A(p)>r this is automatic. If
0<A(p)<=r, set s=A(p), so p=q_A(s) and

    2t-p<=q_C(r-s),

which proves the assertion. If A(p)=0, then p>=q_A(0), and the same
conclusion follows from 2t<=q_A(0)+q_C(r). Hence K(t)>=r.

Conversely, choose a minimizing s in (2), and put p=q_A(s). At t=q
the two endpoint cap volumes sum exactly to r. Thus K(q)<=r. If t>q,
keep p fixed; the C threshold is increased. If r-s>0 its cap volume
strictly decreases, giving K(t)<r. If r-s=0, instead keep the C
threshold fixed at q_C(0) and increase the A threshold; its positive
volume r strictly decreases. Hence K(t)<r for t>q. The strict decrease
of both ordinary quantiles also shows q_K is strictly decreasing: in
(2), use the same mass split proportion at two different positive
values of r. At least one split mass is positive, so at least one
quantile decreases strictly. Continuity and these observations prove
the claimed quantile interpretation and uniqueness.

## 2. Exact d-power concavity

Brunn-Minkowski applied to ordinary parallel caps says A(t)^(1/d) is
concave on its positive support interval, with the constant plateau a
at its left end; likewise for C. Its decreasing inverse

    Q_A(s)=q_A(s^d), 0<=s<=a^(1/d),

is concave. Indeed, if t_i=Q_A(s_i), concavity of the cap-root function
at the convex combination of the t_i gives a value at least the same
convex combination of the s_i. Since it is decreasing, this is
equivalent to Q_A of that combined s being at least the combined t.
The endpoint statement follows by continuity. The same holds for Q_C.

Substitute r=t^d and s=(lambda t)^d in (2). Then

 q_K(t^d)=(1/2) inf_(lambda,kappa>=0, lambda^d+kappa^d=1)
                   [Q_A(lambda t)+Q_C(kappa t)].       (3)

The domain of the infimum is fixed for 0<=t<=a^(1/d). Each function
inside the infimum is concave in t; an infimum of concave functions is
concave, as is seen directly by applying the defining inequality to
each function and then taking its infimum. Thus q_K(t^d) is concave
decreasing. Taking its decreasing inverse once more proves that

    t -> K(t)^(1/d)

is concave throughout {t:K(t)>0}, including its left constant plateau.
The zero region to the right of the support endpoint is not included
in this concavity assertion.

## 3. A compatibility upper bound

If (A+C)/2 is contained in a convex body B, then for every t,

    K(t)<=2 |B intersect {u.x>=t}|.                    (4)

For 0<r<a, formula (2) at its equal split gives

    q_K(r)<= [q_A(r/2)+q_C(r/2)]/2.

The two endpoint caps of volume r/2 at the latter thresholds have a
midpoint body contained in the B cap at their averaged threshold.
Brunn-Minkowski gives this midpoint volume at least r/2. Since q_K(r)
is no larger than that averaged threshold, the B cap at q_K(r) also
has volume at least r/2. For any t, take r<K(t) and use monotonicity
to obtain the same bound at t, then let r increase to K(t). This
includes the saturated value K(t)=a by a limit, and K(t)=0 is trivial.

The full directional depth profile at the middle fiber is
|B intersect {u.x>=t}|+K(t). Its d-th root need not be inferred
concave merely because the two individual d-th roots are concave:
that inference for sums is not valid in general. Equations (2)-(4)
are the proved scalar conclusions here.
